prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor industrial workspace with a concrete floor, a tall wheeled metal wire rack on the left holding flat blue trays, a rectangular cabinet or counter unit on the right (~1.5–3 m away in frame 1, approaching to ~0.8–1.2 m in frame 4), and another person in a red top and dark pants standing between the rack and right-hand unit at roughly 2.5–3.5 m distance. In frames 1 and 2, the metal rack bars and lower blue trays are within arm's reach (~0.4–1.0 m) to the left and below the camera wearer, while the other person is ~1–1.5 m ahead of the rack's far end, facing away and toward the right-hand unit (not looking at the camera wearer) with that unit and stacked blue trays within their arm's reach. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer pitches downward in frame 2 toward the rack, turns rapidly rightward past the rack in frame 3, approaches the right-hand cabinet and the person in frame 4 (where the cabinet partially occludes the person's right side and lower legs), and pitches down in frame 5 where a bright white silhouette at the bottom edge (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach) shows a blue tray held in the camera wearer's hands alongside the rack's bottom wheel on the left (~1.2 m) and stacked blue panels ahead (~1.5–2 m). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the continuous ground-plane gradient, the close proximity of the foreground rack struts in frames 1–2, and the near-field held tray and cabinet box in frames 4–5 much easier to separate from the cluttered background. However, the depth map is completely unreliable in frame 3 where motion blur erases the rack's geometry into a smooth gradient, and it fills in the open gaps between the wire rack bars in frames 1, 2, and 4 as solid surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only a single 'person' class in frames 1 and 4 while leaving all workspace structures, wheeled metal racks, cabinets, and blue trays unsegmented in black across all 5 frames. In frame 1, a pink 'person' mask locates the individual in the red shirt upper-right of center at roughly 3–3.5 m from the camera wearer, bent forward and facing right away from the camera toward the counter unit within their arm's reach, with their lower legs partially occluded by the foreground cabinet and rack wheel. Masks are completely absent in frames 2, 3, and 5 as the camera looks down at the rack (frame 2), sweeps rapidly to the right (frame 3), and looks down at the floor and handheld tray (frame 5). Compared to the cluttered and dimly lit RGB frames, the segmentation map isolates the human figure's silhouette against the busy industrial background in frames 1 and 4. However, the map is highly unreliable: in frame 4 (~2–2.5 m away, where the person faces slightly left/downward next to the right-hand cabinet), the 'person' mask bleeds extensively into the adjacent vertical stack of blue trays and panels to their right and below them, and it fails to segment a distant background person behind the yellow column in frame 1 as well as the camera wearer's own hands and held tray within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) at the bottom of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for either the other person in the workspace or the camera wearer. From the RGB context, a person in a red shirt stands roughly 2.5–3.5 m ahead in frames 1 and 4—facing away and to the right in frame 1 and angled toward the space between the rack and right-hand cabinet in frame 4, never looking directly at the camera wearer—while reaching with their hands toward objects within their arm's reach (~0.5 m) near the cabinet and stacked blue panels. Additionally, in frame 5, as the camera wearer turns past the wheeled wire rack on the left (~1.2 m away) and looks down toward the floor, both of the camera wearer's hands enter the bottom edges of the frame within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) holding a flat blue tray, partially cut off by the lower image boundary. Because no yellow body links or magenta hand keypoints are rendered anywhere in the strip, the pose map adds no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is completely unreliable due to distance, motion blur in frame 3, partial occlusion by the rack and cabinet, and severe truncation of the camera wearer's hands at the bottom edge of frame 5.
